on_9b_nimbus_wall.blurb: Nimbus Wall wraps around the Lion's Head lookout on the Bruce Peninsula and offers some of the more airy lines on the cliff. It holds 14 climbs, a mix of sport and trad with a single aid line, running from about 5.7 up to 5.13. Most of the grades sit in the 5.10 to 5.13 range, so this is a spot for experienced leaders rather than beginners. A handful of routes can be started from the ground, while the rest are reached by rappelling in to a hanging belay from the top of the cliff.

on_the_islands.blurb: The Islands is a maze-like section of The Swamp, a south-facing cliff that gets a mix of sun and shade under heavy tree cover. All 14 routes here are sport climbs, spread fairly evenly between 5.10, 5.11 and 5.12, with several of them regarded as classics of the cliff. There are no easy warm-ups in this section, so it suits climbers already comfortable leading in the 5.10 range and above.

_expect.name: Crescent Moon / Lord of the Flies Wall

on_9g_crescent_moon_lord_of_the_flies_wa.blurb: This wall at Lion's Head on the Bruce Peninsula is a harder-end sport venue. Of its 13 climbs, 12 are bolted and one is trad, and the grades are concentrated between 5.11 and 5.13, with one lone easier line and a single 5.10. Nearly all routes begin on the ground, though a few use hanging belays and some can be reached by rappel. You get here by walking along the cliff from the fourth-class gully or by dropping in from above. It is a destination for strong, confident leaders.

on_9h_mr_bojangles_wall.blurb: Mr. Bojangles Wall is a compact section of Lion's Head on the Bruce Peninsula, with 13 climbs that are mostly sport plus a couple of trad lines. Grades cluster at 5.12, with a good number of 5.11s and a couple of 5.10s, so expect hard single-pitch climbing. Several routes are hanging-belay lines reached by rappelling from the clifftop, and the layout can feel confusing on a first visit. Plan on it being a wall for experienced climbers who are happy with a rope-managed approach.

on_o_the_cat_s_tail.blurb: The Cat's Tail is a small sector of Mount Nemo in the Golden Horseshoe, tucked just beyond the large overhanging Morphine wall. It has 13 routes, with trad lines outnumbering the sport ones. The range is wide, from scrambling-level terrain through the 5.9s and into the low 5.12s, though the bulk of the climbing falls between 5.9 and 5.10. A classic 5.9 trad line gives the sector its name, and a 5.10 sport route is another popular pick, making it a decent stop for climbers who like a bit of both styles.

on_g_alfred_s_wall.blurb: Alfred's Wall is one of the busier sections of Mount Nemo in the Golden Horseshoe, and weekends can bring a crowd. It is mainly a sport wall, with 9 bolted routes and 4 trad lines including a well-liked 5.8. Most climbs fall between 5.10 and 5.11, with a few easier ones below that. The wall sits right beside a slot you scramble down to get there, so the walk is short, but the descent is steep and demands care.

on_orgasmatron_wall.blurb: Orgasmatron Wall is one of five walls at Silver Harbour, a quiet crag near Thunder Bay that has parking beside the lake. It has 13 climbs across sport, trad and top-rope styles, with a spread from around 5.5 to 5.11 that gives beginners and intermediate climbers something to work on. Most routes are bolted, and the harder end tops out at 5.11. The walk in is brief, and this wall is reached by branching off the same path used for a neighbouring wall.
